# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a note early in the game, I signal restraint and cooperation. This establishes credibility and encourages other players to do the same.

When the other players all report fishing their share, I trust that pattern and continue fishing at or slightly above the sustainable share. Cooperation has held; don't break it.

When I calculate my landing, I work from the sustainable share as my baseline, not the full quota. The quota is a ceiling I can breach, but the sustainable share is what keeps the ground alive across all seasons.

When stock is healthy and stable, I land around 8-8.3 per season. This is reliable, won't trigger Coop's retaliation, and accumulates steadily.

When I see another player has landed far above their share (18.0 when sustainable is 8.3), I recognize the ground is under stress but don't retaliate in kind. Instead, I hold my line at reasonable catches to let stock recover.

When stock drops below 85, I don't panic. Sustainable growth still works if everyone stays disciplined. I keep landing around 7-8 per season and let recovery happen.

When I reach the final season, I have one last chance to land. I can take a larger final catch without consequences since the game ends, but only if the stock can bear it. With 64.0 in stock and a sustainable share of 5.3 per boat, I can land up to about half the remaining stock without destroying it for others' final turn.

When tempted to break cooperation, I remember: a crashed fishery scores zero for all remaining seasons. Discipline pays more than greed across the full game length.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a log-book note, I signal "fishing my share" consistently. This establishes trust with the fleet and keeps Coop cooperative.

When the sustainable share and my quota allow comfortable headroom (quota significantly above sustainable share), I fish at or slightly above the sustainable share in the landing stage. This preserves stock while capturing my fair allocation.

When I see all other players consistently fishing their share and stock recovering, I continue the same pattern. Cooperation is self-reinforcing and maximizes total yield across seasons.

When I notice other players landing substantially above their stated share (like Cael landing 18.0 when sustainable share is 7-8), I recognize the ground is under pressure. Do not take this as license to escalate; instead, stay disciplined and land near sustainable levels to prevent stock collapse.

When I reach the final season, I have less incentive to preserve stock for future growth. If the stock is still healthy and I have accumulated less catch than I could have, I may increase my final landing. But only after confirming the stock can sustain it without breaching the rule that no two boats together exceed share plus quota.

When filing a catch amount, verify mentally: would my catch plus any other single boat's catch exceed (sustainable share × 2 + 18)? If yes, reduce my landing.

Do not assume that signaling restraint with a note guarantees others will fish restraint. Watch the actual landings each season and adjust expectations. Notes are cheap signals; landings reveal true intentions.

If stock drops below 80 and is still falling, reconsider whether the cooperative structure is holding. Be prepared to land less aggressively to save the ground rather than race others to the bottom.

2.text:
# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post my log-book note, I commit to a stance that will guide Coop's behavior. If I say "fishing my share," Coop will fish its share and punish overland. Announce cooperation early and maintain it consistently—this is my contract with the rest of the fleet.

When I file a landing, land within or near the sustainable share, not the season quota. The quota of 9 is a ceiling I can approach, but the sustainable share is what keeps the stock healthy. The stock regrows at 50%, so depleting it early cascades into smaller sustainable shares later.

Watch what the other boats actually land, not just what they claim. Notes say one thing; landing logs reveal the truth. If other boats are landing 8+ while calling it "fishing my share" at 8.3, they're truthful. If the fourth boat (Coop's vessel) lands high, that signals the fleet is overfishing and I should adjust down.

On the final landing of each season, do not exceed the sustainable share by more than 0.5-1.0 fish. I landed 8.4 when the share was 5.3 in season 6, thinking I had room within the quota of 9—this was wrong. The sustainable share is the hard boundary for long-term score, not the quota.

In the final season, do not assume I need to maximize that last catch. My score is cumulative across all six seasons. One aggressive final landing that I justified as "within quota" cost me sustainability in earlier seasons and capped my total.

Do not let late-season desperation override the principle: cooperate, land near the sustainable share, keep the stock above 50. My score of 37.9 came from steady landings in the 8+ range, but I could have scored higher by staying below 8 and preserving stock growth across all six seasons.
